active_competency.name: Thiết kế input contract và error semantics cho CLI
active_competency.description: Tạo một command có behavior dự đoán được, lỗi hữu ích và boundary rõ ràng thay vì cố hỗ trợ quá nhiều syntax.

project_snapshot.title: Mini Product Lab
project_snapshot.domain: A rotating set of small non-web developer and operations tools (CLIs, network proxies, background workers, incident fixes) that can be shipped in two or three focused work sessions.
project_snapshot.product_goal: Build useful small software products while practicing specification clarification, implementation judgment, failure handling, and evidence-backed revision.
project_snapshot.architecture_baseline: Local-first CLI, proxy, or small worker implementations selected per mini-project; no web application; use the simplest architecture that satisfies the accepted specification.

weekly_plan.theme: Make a CLI useful under real constraints

project_spec.problem: Developers discover scheduled-job mistakes only after jobs run at the wrong time or overlap in production.
project_spec.user: A developer or operator reviewing a local schedule before deploying it.
functional_requirements: Read a documented local schedule format.
Show the next run time for each valid job.
Report malformed expressions with a useful location and reason.
Warn when two jobs may overlap.
Accept an explicit timezone setting for the analysis.
acceptance_criteria: The same input produces the same output when the timezone is explicit.
An invalid entry does not prevent the user from seeing which other entries are valid.
An overlap warning names both jobs and the relevant time window.
The CLI uses a non-zero exit code when the input cannot be analyzed safely.
The tool does not silently rewrite the schedule.
constraints: Use a small documented subset of cron syntax.
No daemon or background scheduler is required.
No remote service or database is required.
The tool must remain useful on a terminal without color support.
deliverable: A runnable CLI with help text.
Fixtures covering valid input, invalid input, overlap, and timezone behavior.
open_questions: Should a warning affect the exit code or only an error?
How much future should the tool inspect for overlap?
What should happen when a schedule omits its timezone?

boundary.ai_authority: case support and explicitly authorized mechanical work

mini_project.pitch: Build a CLI that explains when scheduled jobs run and warns about likely overlaps.
mini_project.deliverable: A CLI that reads a small schedule file and prints next runs, warnings, and actionable errors.
definition_of_done: A valid schedule produces the next expected run times.
Malformed entries identify the entry and the reason they are invalid.
Potential overlapping jobs are visible with enough context to investigate.
Timezone behavior is stated and demonstrated.
The command exits with useful status codes for valid and invalid input.

history.detail: Mini-project loaded; boundary awaits human acceptance.
Human accepted the active competency and protected scope.
